title: The text discusses the evolution of higher education in Kenya, particularly focusing on the University of Nairobi. It highlights the challenges of accommodating a growing number of students, especially from rural backgrounds, and the historical context of university education in the region. Initially established as the Royal Technical College of East Africa in 1951, it transformed into the University College Nairobi in 1964 and eventually became the University of Nairobi in 1970. The narrative reflects on the increasing demand for university education among indigenous Africans and the political and social dynamics that shaped this educational landscape.
